title: How scissors use levers to cut
examples: Why is thick card easier to cut near the scissor pivot?

explain.say: A pair of scissors is two levers joined by a screw, which is the pivot. Your fingers push on one side of the pivot and the blades cut on the other: a first-class lever, like a seesaw.

draw.text: How scissors use levers to cut

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a lever. Look at the fulcrum, the load and the effort. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: How scissors use levers to cut

explain.say: Your hand squeezes the handles some distance from the pivot. The turning effect, or moment, is the force times that distance.
The card resists close to the pivot. Because the blade's cutting point is four times closer to the pivot than your fingers, it pushes on the card with four times the force.
So slide thick card deep into the scissors, near the screw, for the strongest cut. The blades also slide past each other, shearing the card like a pair of wedges.

faq.a: Yes. Each half of a pair of scissors is a first-class lever: the screw is the pivot, your hand gives the effort on one side, and the card is the load on the other side.
asks: What kind of lever are scissors?

faq.q: Why is thick card easier to cut near the scissor pivot?
faq.a: Cutting near the pivot puts the load close to it while your hand stays far away. The moments balance, so the blade pushes much harder than your fingers.
asks: Where should I cut with scissors?

faq.a: The two sharp blades slide closely past each other. They push the material from opposite sides until it shears, which is why the blades must be tight together.
asks: Why do loose scissors not cut?

faq.q: Why do garden shears have long handles?
faq.a: Long handles put your hands far from the pivot, giving a big moment, so the short blades can cut through thick stems.
asks: Why do bolt cutters have long handles?

faq.a: A moment is the turning effect of a force, equal to the force times its distance from the pivot. A lever balances when the moments on each side are equal.
asks: What is the law of moments?

facts: Scissors are a pair of first-class levers sharing one pivot.
At balance, effort times its distance from the pivot equals load times its distance.

quiz.say: Your fingers are 8 cm from the pivot and the card is 2 cm from it. How many times your squeeze does the blade push with?
quiz.show: Your fingers are 8 cm from the pivot and the card is 2 cm from it. How many times your squeeze does the blade push with?
quiz.why: 8 divided by 2 is 4, so the force on the card is four times your squeeze.

wrong.0: That is the card's distance, not the ratio.
wrong.2: Multiplying the distances is not the rule; divide them.
